records.explanation:
Wilting is the drooping of leaves and stems caused by loss of turgidity in plant cells.
It is produced when water loss through transpiration exceeds water uptake by the roots, so cells lose their internal pressure (turgor).
That loss of turgor in whole organs makes tissues limp and droop; if water is restored quickly the condition can reverse, but prolonged imbalance causes permanent damage.
Answer: Wilting

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
Mollusca are soft-bodied and usually unsegmented, matching the question’s description.
Many molluscs have an external shell made mainly of calcium carbonate that protects their soft body.
The mantle is the organ that secretes this CaCO3 shell, fitting the “enclosed in a calcium carbonate shell” part.
Answer: Mollusca

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
Solar radiation
Green plants capture solar radiation with chlorophyll and use it in photosynthesis to build organic molecules.
Those organic molecules store chemical energy that fuels herbivores and then higher trophic levels.
Because sunlight is the external energy input driving primary productivity, solar radiation is the ultimate source powering terrestrial food webs.

records.explanation:
Height shows a continuous range of values in people, with many intermediate statures rather than a few discrete categories.
This occurs because height is polygenic, with many genes each contributing small effects that add together.
Environmental factors such as nutrition and health further modify height, producing an approximately bell-shaped distribution in a population.
Correct answer: Height

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
Discontinuous variation means traits that fall into distinct categories with no intermediate forms.
The ABO blood group assigns people to discrete types A, B, AB or O rather than a continuous range.
These separate blood types come from different alleles at a single gene locus (A and B are co‑dominant, O is recessive), producing distinct phenotypes.
Final answer: Blood group

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
Thylakoid membrane, grana
The light-dependent reactions occur on the thylakoid membranes where photosystems I and II absorb light.
Those membranes contain the electron transport chain and ATP synthase that produce ATP and NADPH and release O2.
Grana are stacked thylakoids that increase membrane surface area to hold many pigment-protein complexes, improving light capture and electron transport efficiency.

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
Mitochondria contain their own circular DNA (a mitochondrial genome) inside the organelle.
They replicate that DNA and divide by binary fission, so they can reproduce independently of the nucleus.
This semi-autonomy allows them to synthesise some of their own proteins and maintain their energy-producing functions.
Mitochondrion

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
Absence of a digestive system and direct absorption of digested food
Taenia solium lacks a mouth and gut, so it cannot digest food internally.
Its tegument is syncytial and covered with microtriches, which greatly increase surface area for absorbing nutrients.
This direct absorption of host-digested nutrients is the key structural adaptation for its parasitic lifestyle.

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
Aortic semilunar valve
It is located at the junction between the left ventricle and the aorta where blood leaves the heart.
When the left ventricle relaxes (diastole) the valve cusps close to stop retrograde flow from the high-pressure aorta into the ventricle.
Because it forms a one-way seal at that junction to prevent backflow into the left ventricle, it is the correct valve.

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
Aldosterone is a mineralocorticoid hormone produced by the adrenal cortex that controls sodium and potassium balance in blood plasma.
It acts mainly on the kidney's distal tubules and collecting ducts to increase sodium reabsorption and promote potassium excretion.
These renal effects directly change plasma Na+ and K+ concentrations, maintaining electrolyte balance.
Answer: Aldosterone

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
ADH increases the permeability of the collecting duct to water.
It does so by inserting aquaporin channels into the membranes of principal cells in the collecting duct.
Water then moves by osmosis into the medullary interstitium and peritubular capillaries, enabling ADH-stimulated water reabsorption.
Collecting duct

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
Pancreatic lipase hydrolyses emulsified triglycerides in the small intestine.
It cleaves the ester bonds of triglycerides to produce free fatty acids and glycerol (in practice often monoglycerides plus fatty acids).
Bile salt emulsification increases the surface area of fat droplets so pancreatic lipase can access and efficiently break down the fats.
Final answer: Pancreatic lipase

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
Mosquito
Female mosquitoes have a needle-like proboscis made of stylets (modified mandibles and maxillae) enclosed in a labium sheath.
These piercing–sucking mouthparts are specialized to penetrate tissue and draw up blood or plant fluids.
Because of this structural modification for piercing and sucking, mosquito is the correct choice.

Correct answer: Climax community
This is the final, relatively stable and self-sustaining assemblage of species reached through succession.
Once established, species composition stays largely unchanged over time unless disrupted by a major disturbance.
Because it is the stable end-point of succession, it matches the question's description.

records.explanation:
Negative geotropism
It means shoots grow upward, away from the direction of gravity.
This upward curvature happens because auxin is redistributed in the shoot, causing differential cell elongation on opposite sides.
Final answer: Negative geotropism

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
The diaphragm is a dome-shaped sheet of muscle that moves upward when it relaxes.
This upward bulging reduces thoracic cavity volume and increases intrapulmonary pressure.
The higher pressure forces air out of the lungs, producing exhalation.
Correct answer: Dome-shaped

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
Male and female organs maturing at different times
This temporal separation (dichogamy) means anthers shed pollen at a different time from when the stigma is receptive.
Because male and female parts are not mature together, a flower’s own pollen is unlikely to fertilize its ovules.
This reduced self-fertilization raises the chance that pollen from other flowers will succeed, so cross-pollination is favored.

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
In a test cross Tt × tt, the heterozygote Tt produces equal T and t gametes.
The homozygous recessive parent tt produces only t gametes.
Half the zygotes are Tt (expressing the dominant trait) and half are tt (expressing the recessive trait).
Therefore the phenotypic ratio is 1:1.

records.sourceLabel: Owner-provided Biology non-diagram collection — pending provenance review
records.explanation:
Phloem sieve tubes
These living conduits carry sucrose and other organic solutes from photosynthetic leaves to storage tissues over long distances.
Companion cells actively load sucrose into sieve elements, increasing osmotic concentration and drawing water in.
The resulting pressure-driven mass flow (pressure-flow mechanism) moves the sucrose-rich sap toward sinks for storage.

records.explanation:
Carbon dioxide
It is the largest long-lived human-caused greenhouse gas whose atmospheric concentration has risen sharply from fossil fuel use and land-use change.
CO2 molecules absorb and re-radiate outgoing infrared radiation, increasing the heat retained in the atmosphere and producing an enhanced greenhouse effect.
Because CO2 is long-lived and directly controlled by emissions, its rise is the primary human-driven cause of recent global warming.
